description: Start a film: from a template (recommended: it comes cut, with transitions, music and sounds), empty, or as a copy of another film (from: a film of its own, to try a variant — another order of scenes, another style, another language — without touching the original). Give the brand here or later with set_brand; with site, Cutscene reads it, with pictures of the product's pages, from its public site. The film is a .cutscene.json file in the working folder; the same file opens in the Cutscene editor.

colors.description: bg = background, surface = cards, ink = text, muted = quiet text, accent = the brand's colour (key words, buttons), accent2 = a second colour (a word that turns on a ground of the brand's colour, a second dot). Left out, accent2 is a deep shade of accent

fonts.description: Font families of the library (see the guide resource for the list)

format.description: 16:9 (default), 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1. Can change later: shots recompose themselves

from.description: A film to copy instead (its name): the copy keeps its shots, words, brand and format, and takes name (and title, when given) only

lang.description: Language of the example words (default en)

logo.description: Path of a logo file on this machine (SVG or PNG on a transparent ground; the empty room around the mark is cut off), or null for none

montage.description: A montage id (see list_montages), or a template people shared (search_community). Without one the film is empty

name.description: A short name for the file, e.g. launch-acme

product.description: The product's name and tagline, used by the montage where it shows them

radius.description: Corner radius of cards and screens: 4 sharp, 16 soft, 28 round

site.description: The product's public web address (https://monproduit.com). Cutscene reads it: the name, the logo, the colours and the fonts, and pictures of its home page and of up to two pages it links to (features, product), put in the shots that show a screen and still wait for a picture. Only a site the user has the right to use (their own product's). What you give besides (brand_name, colors, fonts, logo) wins over what the site says. The answer says what was found and what was not: ask the user for the rest

title.description: The film's title (default: the product's name, else the file's name)

name: create_film
title: Create a film
